newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: KORAM ASKED TO STEP UP CREDIT SCREENING.
newsitem.headline: KORAM ASKED TO STEP UP CREDIT SCREENING.

text.p: The central Bank of Korea has asked Koram Bank to strengthen its credit analysis, the BOK said in an annual inspection report released on Friday.
It said Koram needed to be more cautious in screening companies and granting loans.
Moreover, Koram should write more detailed credit evaluations and make sure to report any credit-related information to the Korea Federation of Banks.
Koram's total assets rose to 12.12 trillion won by the end of April, up 27.7 percent from a year earlier, according to the report.
Its 1996 net profit was tallied at 28.8 billion won, up 76.7 percent from a year ago, it said.
The bank's weighted bad loan ratio fell to 1.1 percent at the end of 1996, against 1.3 percent a year ago.
